newsitem.title: CANADA: More than 30,000 Quebec govt' employees in buyout.
newsitem.headline: More than 30,000 Quebec govt' employees in buyout.

text.p: More than 30,000 Quebec public sector employees, twice the number expected, accepted the province's early retirement offer, Quebec government officials said on Friday.
The early retirement program is part of Quebec's plan to eliminate its budget deficit by the year 2000.
The government said that 29,917 employees entered the "voluntary retirement plan" and that 222 other applicants would likely be approved.
Quebec had targeted C$800 million in annual savings starting next year if 15,000 employees took the early retirement offer.
Quebec's Treasury Board will announce in September the level of savings expected from the greater than expected retirements.

"We know that we will go beyond our objective, but we don't know by how much," Treasury Board spokesman Pierre-Jules Poulin told Reuters. "We have to replace some of the employees leaving. But in education, for instance, new workers will cost half as much as those who are leaving."
Among retiring employees are 14,087 health care workers and 12,198 teachers and other education workers. Only 3,632 are actual civil servants.
